findings.result_name: Evaluation is cheap: at most d(G)+2 <= |C|+2 strategy evaluations
findings.defect: The last sentence of the statement -- "The same bound and the same proof hold for the profile oracle, which takes a positional PAIR and returns val_{sigma,tau}" (rem:qm-profile: "holds verbatim ... The rank argument is unchanged") -- is FALSE. In the profile model the recorded points are val_pi|_C for arbitrary profiles pi in {0,1}^C, which need not lie in aff{val_sigma|_C}; the rank argument therefore bounds the non-halting queries by d_pi(G)+1, where d_pi(G):=dim aff{val_pi|_C : pi in {0,1}^C}, NOT by d(G)+1. d_pi > d(G) is the rule, not the exception, and the gap is realised by actual runs.
findings.evidence: REFUTED BY THE ROUTE'S OWN CODE. Five-vertex stopping SSG kinds=['max','min','min'], succ=[(3,3),(4,2),(4,0)] (n=3, t0=3, t1=4; stopping by the trap test; w* = (0,0,0)). Here d(G)=0 (v0's two successors are both t0, so val_sigma|_C = (0,0,0) for both sigma), so the claimed bound is d(G)+2 = 2. Running the route's own /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/r17-query-model/qm.py learn_profile on it gives 3 queries, log [(1,[2],0,1),(2,[1],1,2),(3,[],2,3)] -- the rank reaches 3 = d_pi+1 with d_pi = 2. A random search over the route's learn_profile found 3 violations in the first 4 stopping two-player games tested (routecopy/search.py, seed 5: q=3 vs d=0; q=4 vs d=0; q=3 vs d=0). Independently, my own reimplementation of Algorithm E's profile variant (exact rationals, hypothesis = a consistent harmonic system verified substochastic and with empty full-mass set) takes 4 queries with d(G)=1 (bound 3) on the 7-vertex game kinds=['min','avg','max','min','max'], succ=[(4,1),(6,5),(0,1),(6,0),(1,6)]; the four rounds, their harmonic systems, greedy pairs and value vectors are printed and hand-checkable (round 3 rows: (0,0)=(0,{2:1}), (2,0)=(0,{4:1}), (3,1)=(0,{4:1}), rest constant; d_pi = 4). The |C|+2 bound survives in every case (4 <= 6, 3 <= 5), and the route's own verification field only ever checked |C|+2 for the profile variant, which is why this was missed. Files: routecopy/search.py, prof.py, profadv.py.

findings.result_name: Values beat orientations: a strict separation of the evaluation and outmap oracles
findings.defect: Q_out(S) = 4 is wrong for the family as constructed, and the proof's reduction step ("an outmap algorithm for S is an outmap algorithm for the class of all AUSOs of the 3-cube") is invalid under the route's own def:qm-oracle, which states that an evaluation algorithm is GIVEN the controlled skeleton Sigma(G), including "which are sinks". The eighteen games of prop:m3-realised / prop:m3-one-min do not share a skeleton: 8 of the 16 one-player realisations have a Max vertex one of whose actions is the sink t0, and the two non-Holt-Klee realisations carry a Min vertex. Sigma therefore partitions the 728 AUSOs before any query is made, and every bucket is solvable in 3 outmap queries.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from the game files in /data/ssg-proof/scripts/round16-verify/m3games. Skeleton shapes (exact, from the JSON): game_m3_01234576, 01235674, 01237456, 01325476, 01325674, 01326745, 01327645, 01327654 each have a Max vertex with successor t0; the other 8 one-player games have none; G_m3_k1_a (145 vertices) and G_m3_k1_b (86) each have one Min vertex. Under the order-48 group the 8 sink-free classes have orbit union of 320 AUSOs and the 8 sink-carrying classes 336 (656 = HK total, verified). Two independently written exact minimax computations (cubes.py memoised, dout2.py memo-free iterative deepening) both give: D_out(all 728) = 4, D_out(656 HK) = 4, D_out(320 sink-free bucket) = 3, D_out(336 union) = 3, D_out(72 non-HK) = 3. An explicit 3-query decision tree for the 320-bucket is printed (first query at vertex 0, then 1/2/3/4/5/6, then one more). D_out is monotone under subsets, so every finer Sigma-bucket is <= 3; hence Q_out(S) = 3, not 4. Everything else in the proposition reproduces: I rebuilt SEP independently (theta(z) = (2 idx(z)+1)/32 as a 5-vertex dyadic chain, h -> (t1,t0)) on G_m3_k1_a and on all eight sink-relocations by successor swaps -- N = 152, stopping, 0 tied incidences, orientation exactly the product of s with the combed 1-cube, sink (1,z), theta constant over all 16 strategies and equal to theta(z), so Q(S) = 1 is correct. The statement is repairable (replace each sink successor of a Max vertex by a fresh average vertex -> (t0,t0), which changes no value, keeps the game stopping and makes Sigma uniform over the 656 HK-realising members), but as written the claimed 4 is false and the reduction is asserted against the model's own definition. Files: sep2.py, cubes.py, dout2.py, hk.py.

findings.result_name: Evaluation is cheap: at most d(G)+2 <= |C|+2 strategy evaluations
findings.defect: The third framing remark after def:qm-oracle, "the halting test is free ... and Q is unchanged if we demand one [a certificate]", is false, and is refuted by the route's own family HDP_m.
findings.evidence: Exact minimax over decision trees on the HDP answer structure (the answer at sigma is a function of (sigma,i), proved in thm:qm-hdp(b) and verified by me): Q without a certificate = 1,2,3,4,5 for m = 1..5; Q when the algorithm must have made a query returning S_sigma = empty = 2,3,4,5,6. The adversary keeps a prefix and never answers i = m+1 while |p| < m, so the optimum is known after m queries but is only certified by an (m+1)-st. This does not propagate: thm:qm-eval's Algorithm E produces a certificate, so its bound holds in both models, and thm:qm-hdp's lower bound is proved in the weaker model.

findings.result_name: Evaluation is not free: the hidden decision path HDP_m needs |Vmax| queries
findings.defect: cor:qm-theta, "|Vmax| <= Q <= |C|+2 over the stopping SSGs with a given controlled set", is false as a universally quantified statement over controlled sets/skeletons; the lower bound is a property of the HDP skeleton (and of any class containing HDP_m), not of every controlled set.
findings.evidence: Counterexample to the quantifier: take the skeleton in which every Max vertex has successors (t0,t1) and there are no Min vertices. Every stopping SSG with that skeleton has the same unique optimal strategy (point at t1), so a correct evaluation algorithm outputs it with 0 queries; Q = 0 < |Vmax| for every m. The correct statement is "there is a family with a single controlled skeleton and |Vmax| = m on which Q >= m", which is what thm:qm-hdp proves and what I verified (exact minimax Q(HDP_m) = m for m = 1..6).

findings.result_name: Evaluation is not free: the hidden decision path HDP_m needs |Vmax| queries
findings.defect: The randomised half of thm:qm-hdp(c) uses, without proof, a fifth imported fact: "a tree with branching <= b and L leaves has average leaf depth at least log_b L". Rule 4 forbids a fifth import; the route flags the attribution ("Shannon's") only in the prior_art field, not as a GAP, and does not prove it.
findings.evidence: The step is the only non-elementary ingredient of the expected-query bound m/log_2(m+1). It is repairable in three lines (Kraft: sum over leaves of b^{-d_i} <= 1 by induction on the tree; then AM-GM gives b^{-(1/L) sum d_i} <= (1/L) sum b^{-d_i} <= 1/L, i.e. average depth >= log_b L), so the statement is true, but as submitted it is asserted.

findings.result_name: Evaluation is cheap: at most d(G)+2 <= |C|+2 strategy evaluations
findings.defect: Algorithm E is not a deterministic algorithm as written: "Choose a harmonic system rho-hat on Sigma(G) consistent with D" names no function, and the set of consistent systems satisfying def:qm-harmonic's stopping condition is a polytope MINUS a union of faces, so it is not closed and a linear-programming selection can land outside it. The route's own choose_hypothesis raises RuntimeError('no consistent stopping hypothesis found') in exactly that case.
findings.evidence: In my reimplementation, random-objective selections landed outside the stopping condition on essentially every trial for L_2..L_4, G*, HDP (0 valid trials out of 60 per game), so the failure mode is real and common. The theorem is still true -- a canonical selection exists: take, for each row (v,a), the barycentre of its consistency polytope; if the barycentre system had a full-mass set U, then q=0 and |p|_1=1 would be tight at a relative-interior point, so the whole polytope, rho_G included, would lie in that face, and supp p_G is contained in supp p_barycentre, so rho_G would have the same full-mass set, contradicting lem:qm-form(a). This repair is asserted nowhere in the route.

findings.result_name: No evaluation-model barrier: the paper's exponential lower bounds carry no information
findings.defect: Two rhetorical inaccuracies. (a) "the same instances would be solved by |C|+2 evaluations of the very operation those rules perform once per round" is wrong for the calculi: a round of M2 (def:slack), M2T, M4 (def:transport), M5 (sec:hybrid) or M6 (def:ratio) is a propagation step, not a strategy evaluation, so H_m, WD, CC and CV are not families on which a rule performs one evaluation per round. (b) For those same families |C| is 1 (H_m), 2 (WD, CC) or 3 (CV), so "solved by |C|+2 evaluations" is near-vacuous there -- a game with one controlled vertex is solved by trying both actions.
findings.evidence: |C| recomputed from the builders: myinst.H_m(2..5) has |C| = 1; wd.WD(2,2,4)/(2,3,5)/(3,4,7) and cc.CC(2,3)/(6,7)/(10,11) have |C| = 2; cv_build.CV(1,4)/(3,4)/(5,4) has |C| = 3. The evaluation counts themselves reproduce exactly (1 query each), as do L_2/L_4/L_6/L_8 = 3/5/7/8.

verdict:
Two major defects survive, so the route is not sound as submitted; the central theorem is, however, correct and I could not break it.

WHAT I REBUILT AND CONFIRMED (all exact rational, independent code in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/d1fe2115-9b72-4784-bb94-87421ac1106c/scratchpad/r17-audit-query-model-correctness/, written from the statements). (1) lem:qm-form: the three parts reconstructed and found correct (absorption a.s.; a full-mass set plus the average vertices below it is a nonempty trap, contradicting lem:trapchar; optional stopping at the hitting time of C u {t0,t1}; S^n 1 -> 0 and the domination |T^n y - T^n y'| <= S^n|y-y'|). My independent harmonic() reproduces the paper's printed normal form of W_10 in thm:lasserre-vacuous exactly: v1 (e_2;0),(e_3;0); v2 (0;1/2),(7/8 e_1;0); v3 (0;1/4),(7/8 e_1;0). (2) thm:qm-eval for the Max-strategy oracle: the rank step -- the heart of the proof -- is correct, and I asserted rank(V_{t+1}) = rank(V_t)+1 inside every run: 120 random two-player stopping games plus 480 adversarial runs with randomised consistent selections, 0 failures, 0 wrong outputs, 0 runs above d(G)+2, worst q-|C| = 1. Query counts reproduce the route's exactly: L_2/L_4/L_6/L_8 = 3/5/7/8, G8 = 2, H_2..H_5 = 1, G* = 2, WD = 1, CC = 1, CV = 1, B1 = 1, B2_small = 5, H5 = 4, TB_D10 = 5; d(G) = |C| for the ladders, RC, HDP, B2_small, H5, TB_D10, d = 4 < 7 for G*, d = 1 for CV. (3) thm:qm-hdp (a),(b) and the deterministic half of (c): verified for every one of the 2^m members at m = 2,3,4,5 -- stopping by the trap test, exactly ONE controlled skeleton across all members, values 1/4 + 2^{-j-1} for j < i and 1/4 for j >= i, S_sigma = {v_i}, Opt = {z}, and the full name-indexed answer constant on every (sigma,i) bucket with 0 clashes; the exact minimax query complexity of the class is m for m = 1..6. (4) cor:qm-runs: L_3/L_4/L_5/L_6 give 8/16/32/64 rounds with 4/5/6/7 rank-adding and 4/11/26/57 predicted, and at every predicted round six different consistent harmonic systems all reproduced the value vector and all 2|C| appeals exactly -- 0 mispredictions. (5) The cube census and the m=3 realisations: 744/728 USOs/AUSOs, 18 acyclic classes whose orbits cover exactly 728, D_out = 1,2,4 at m = 1,2,3 by two independent minimax implementations; the eighteen game files recomputed FROM THE GAME (val_sigma as the componentwise minimum over all Min strategies) are all stopping, tie-free, acyclic USOs with the stored outmaps, <= 1 Min vertex, <= 145 vertices; SEP built independently on all eight sink corners is stopping, tie-free, N = 152, orientation the product with the combed 1-cube, sink (1,z), theta decoding z from one evaluation.

WHAT BREAKS. (i) The profile-oracle clause of thm:qm-eval is false: the correct bound is d_pi(G)+2 (profile-value dimension), not d(G)+2, and the route's own qm.py exceeds d(G)+2 on a 5-vertex game. (ii) prop:qm-separation's Q_out(S) = 4 is wrong for the family as constructed -- def:qm-oracle hands the algorithm Sigma(G), the eighteen cited realisations do not share a skeleton (8 of 16 expose a t0 successor at a Max vertex; 2 carry a Min vertex), and every skeleton bucket has D_out = 3, so Q_out(S) = 3. Both are repairable and neither touches the headline |C|+2 upper bound or the HDP lower bound; the standing-error checklist (greedy policy iteration, dict-literal row collapse, sinks as sentinels, t0 in the trap, unpinned sinks, non-dyadic witnesses, polynomial-class smuggling) turned up nothing, and the model uses no target-equivalent oracle -- val_sigma is polynomial by thm:eval-stopfree, and rem:qm-eval correctly discloses that the hypothesis-solving step is itself SSG-hard.
